findings.reason: Confirmed against the exact fourteen listed duplicate entries and the full consumer stage descriptions: these stages apply or verify arithmetic hypotheses for the abstract algebra owner, including PA.4’s express handoff. Remove the listed pairs from duplicates and retain any useful consumer links as such. This does not certify every unchallenged duplicate as genuine; no such extra claim is needed for this correction.

Confirmed. Read TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Integral.lean:57,76 with its section variables. The integral dimension inequality has no injectivity assumption; equality requires FaithfulSMul, hence an injective algebra map. Add these finite-map ingredients while keeping the composite depth/dimension target partial. Do not claim equality for arbitrary finite maps.

Confirmed, with a precise status fix. Evaluation.lean opens WithPiTopology and eval₂_unique explicitly assumes continuity in that topology. The complete-local specialization needs the adic/Pi topology and continuity assembly as well as IsAdic.isAdicComplete_iff and MvPowerSeries.hasEval_of_mem (both read with hypotheses). For the intended maximal-ideal-adic target, mark it partial until that assembly is supplied; the generic Pi-topological universal property itself remains available.

Confirmed. Completeness.lean:213–214 completes with respect to the variable-generated ideal, whereas the local-ring instance is Inverse.lean:152. Neither is a maximal-ideal-adic completeness theorem over a complete local coefficient ring. Correct the topology qualifier and cite the local instance; retain partial status.

Confirmed. GoingUp.lean:327 gives an over-prime for an integral map provided I.comap≤P; at I=0,P=0 this requires injectivity. Tau Ceti supplies the integral dimension inequality. These are omitted ingredients, not the full characteristic-zero point theorem. Retain the non-torsion/dimension and finite-extension realization obligations.

Confirmed. LocalRing/Module.lean:112 is the stated finite-module fibre criterion. For q over p, the fibre of B⊗M is the scalar extension to κ(q) of κ(p)⊗M; field extension is faithfully flat and detects its nonvanishing. Thus for finite M the support equality holds along any ring map. Cite this ingredient and retain partial status for the whole transport/framing target.

Confirmed. HasSubst is algebraic nilpotence of the constant coefficient, while HasEval is topological nilpotence. PowerSeries.aeval, continuous_aeval and comp_aeval have the complete separated linear-topology hypotheses the re-expansion needs. Tau Ceti aeval_subst still assumes HasSubst: it is a compatibility result on that smaller domain, not a way to remove the nilpotence hypothesis. Construct the p-adic maps through evaluation; retain the actual completeness/continuity and cocycle assembly.

Confirmed with the characteristic qualification restored. Over Z, P₁=1−X already refutes monicity, and the leading coefficient is (−1)^N. Divide by the monic associate (−1)^N P_N, generating the same ideal. The final proposed sentence that %ₘ is the identity for every odd N needs −1≠1 in R: in characteristic 2 the polynomial is monic. modByMonic only returns its input in the nonmonic case.

Confirmed after reading Habiro printed 1134–1135 and the pinned characteristic-p cyclotomic formulas. Mapping the integral polynomial identity to ZMod p yields the congruence; the p-divisible case iterates cyclotomic_mul_prime_dvd_eq_pow. This does not supply the integral ideal containment (4.2) or the general resultant/comaximality theorem. Retain the n≠2 norm hypothesis (and the stated cyclotomic-extension/irreducibility assumptions).

Confirmed with a zero-ring boundary correction. For nonempty S⊂positive integers choose n∈S; divisibility by every Φ_n^k contradicts the finite degree of any nonzero polynomial, using the read monic-degree lemmas. No domain or p-adic separation hypothesis is needed. For S empty the target is the zero ring and the map fails to be injective when R is nontrivial; for the zero coefficient ring it is injective. The stage’s generic caution was not itself a false assertion, but the audit should give this exact elementary criterion.

Confirmed. GroupCompletion.instModule and ContinuousLinearMap.completion work for arbitrary uniform additive modules with uniformly continuous scalar actions, not just one adic ideal. The cyclotomic module can reuse them after constructing its uniformity. Keep completed-ring scalars and inverse-limit comparison as assembly obligations. Generic product-completion machinery also exists (AbstractCompletion.prod), so do not describe the finite-product topology itself as absent merely because the specialized module equivalence is not packaged.

Confirmed with an explicit fixed-domain construction. For ζ of order d∈S, project the Habiro completion to R[q]/(Φ_d^n), then use q↦ζ+X modulo X^n: Φ_d(ζ+X) has zero constant term, so its nth power vanishes there. These give compatible maps from the same completed source into R[ζ][[X]]/(X^n). Apply IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom with that source and the read X-adic completeness instance. Arbitrary f need not vanish modulo X^n; the proposed shorthand R[q]/(f) must use factors divisible by Φ_d^n. No cofinality of this single-root family in the full cyclotomic system is needed.

Confirmed. If n is a unit then X^n−1 is separable; for distinct positive d,e dividing n, Φ_dΦ_e divides its cyclotomic factorization, so Separable.of_dvd and Separable.isCoprime give comaximality. This applies to p-power orders over Z[1/p]. It is a compositional library proof, not a new cyclotomic resultant theorem. Additional orders not covered by the unit condition still need their appropriate arithmetic argument.

Confirmed. Read the seven polynomial declarations with their variables: division and remainder are ingredients in the completed expansion, while Taylor/Hasse identities describe polynomial inputs. None states the completed target. Use related for division and special case for the polynomial identities; keep partial status. A bare derivative definition can also be labelled related rather than claiming an exact completed theorem.

Do not classify HB.4’s convergence or asymptotic expansion as duplicate completion theory. The existing ordinary Pochhammer file has q-Pochhammer as a TODO.

Confirmed. Read AdjoinRoot.equivPiFactors, isSeparable_of_separable and projFactor, Polynomial.Factors.linearEquivRoots, and the cyclotomic separability/squarefreeness statements. They provide the omitted finite-field algebra decomposition. Confirmed for the intended cyclotomic re-expansions. eval₂Hom and hasSum_eval₂ accept topological nilpotence in a complete Hausdorff linearly topologised ring; HasSubst requires algebraic nilpotence. Correct the finding’s ancillary generalization: p-torsion-free alone does not imply reduced (Z_p[ε]/ε² is a counterexample), so nonzero does not by itself imply nonnilpotent. In the intended reduced cyclotomic coefficient domains the distinction applies. Retain compatible root choices, topology and convergence hypotheses.

Confirmed as a shared abstract-interface ownership gap, not duplication of the whole higher-K operations construction. The full HR.1, Z.3 and S.6 descriptions require compatible lambda/Adams laws, and a whole-tree search finds only lambda-ring TODO/documentation, not an abstract definition. Z.3’s general lambda-ring axioms must handle torsion; the torsion-free Adams characterization is a restricted comparison. Name one owner for that common interface. Higher Adams operations on K-groups and their weight/boundary laws remain S.6-specific; identical composition notation alone does not make their constructions duplicates.

Confirmed with the coefficient restriction explicit. Read expand, expand_one, expand_mul, map_expand and map_frobenius_expand. They supply the toric polynomial operations over Z, whose reduction has Frobenius-fixed F_p coefficients. Over an arbitrary coefficient ring expand fixes coefficients, and the stated theorem includes map (frobenius R p); expand alone need not satisfy the Frobenius congruence. Preserve the base lambda-structure and Laurent/free-structure assembly obligations.

Confirmed. SqrtFive.lean declares [NeZero (2 : E)] before both factorization and reducibility theorems. The unrestricted audit sentence drops that hypothesis. Characteristic11 is allowed and 4²=5 there; characteristic 2 is a genuine counterexample to the unqualified sentence.

Confirmed. The norm theorem read at PrimitiveRoots.lean:360 requires its cyclotomic-extension and irreducibility assumptions and n≠2. Keep the actual completed intersection argument separate.

Confirmed as a statement-expressibility correction. Abelian.Ext is defined with HasExt; enough projectives supplies HasExt with the required local-smallness universe. Vanishing for a module includes Ext⁰, not just positive degrees; for complexes use all shifts. AdicCompletion can be formed on the tensor product after explicitly transporting the A-action along σ. Neither observation supplies the derived completion functor, the intended Adams/Frobenius maps or their comparison theorem.

Confirmed with a scope limit. The quoted integration remark belongs to Algebra/Order/Interval/Basic.lean. State the nonsingularity restriction on existence, not on uniqueness.
